evidence: Applicability: the product is heavily interactive and time-varying (instruction.md:3-7; hireops_rules.md:82-85 optimistic move/put-back, 115-123 live updates within 15 s preserving typing/focus/card/scroll, 136-147 Enter/Shift+Enter and paged history keeping place, 156-160 scrolled-up arrival, 168-175 drafts across reload/session end). Responsive and themed behaviour is explicitly out of scope (instruction.md:11 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'), and visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required', so no resize/toggle is owed. Every interactive/time-varying criterion tells the judge to act and wait rather than score a first paint: (1) Live board - functional/prompt.md:47 protocol V 'In an independent context Mei Lin moves a J1 card and adds a new J1 card. Without reloading or clicking in this page, wait up to 15 seconds (a wait-for call, or snapshots; accept what is present at the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds)'; criterion hro_live_board functional/judge.toml:290. (2) Live preservation - polish/judge.toml:23 hro_pol_live_board: open card details, click into note box, type 'Call back on Fri', scroll page or board container (with a fallback 'add cards until one does'), other recruiter moves a card, then check details open, note value, document.activeElement, scroll offset and that typing appends; polish/prompt.md:14 'After that action do not reload, navigate, click or type in the observed page until the update has been seen or 15 seconds have passed. Read document.activeElement, field values and scroll offsets with page.evaluate'. (3) Live thread - polish/judge.toml:32 hro_pol_live_thread: type unfinished reply, Noor sends, check draft, focus, append, view at newest. (4) Paged history place - polish/judge.toml:41 hro_pol_earlier_place uses getBoundingClientRect().top before/after loading earlier messages; functional hro_thread_latest/hro_thread_earlier (judge.toml:317,326) open and repeatedly load. (5) Scrolled-up arrival - functional/prompt.md:41 'as Rafael scroll up to earlier messages, then as Noor (independent context) send a message; read Rafael's place, the notice and the unread count before and after he goes to it'; criterion judge.toml:344. (6) Unread/seen live - functional/prompt.md:41 'Every reading in U is made without reloading, navigating or clicking in Rafael's page: wait up to 15 seconds after the other person acts (accept the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds)'; criteria hro_unread_counts judge.toml:335, hro_seen judge.toml:353, hro_msg_exchange judge.toml:299 ('appears on Rafael's open conversation within 15 seconds without reload'). (7) Keyboard behaviour - hro_msg_compose judge.toml:308 Shift+Enter/Enter and box empty+focused afterwards; hro_refused_put_back judge.toml:137 reads document.activeElement after the refused full-Interview move. (8) Drafts across navigation and reload - functional/prompt.md:39 'Type an unsent reply, open a different conversation and the Board, come back, reload, and read the box each time'; hro_drafts judge.toml:371. (9) Failed send and ended session - polish/judge.toml:50 aborts one send via route/setOffline and resends; :59 ends session in a second tab, then presses Enter/Send in the first page and checks the sign-in prompt and draft resume. (10) Restart - functional/prompt.md:51 restart_app then compare. Timing semantics are consistent across brief (15 s), rules and prompt ('first snapshot at or after 15 seconds'), so a conforming app polling at ~15 s is not penalised by a sub-second race. Weak-app reasoning: a static first-paint board, an app that only refreshes on click/focus, or an app that reloads the page every few seconds would each be caught (V/U forbid clicking; hro_pol_live_board checks note value, activeElement and scroll after the update; hro_pol_live_thread checks draft/focus). Conforming alternatives (SSE, WebSocket or polling; any route/labels; no scroll container at the viewport) are accommodated (hireops_rules.md:123; polish/judge.toml:23 no-scroll fallback; app_context.md:33-34). Visual Likert rows are read-only still review by design (visual/prompt.md:14) but do require an open card, an open long conversation and the candidate view, not just the first paint; they grade craft, not interactive behaviour, which is graded in functional/polish. Golden scripted evidence (hashes verified against raw-evidence-index.json) shows the live behaviours exist to be exercised: workspace.json group 17 'live board: another person's move arrives without reload; open card, note draft and focus kept; draft survives reload' passed with arrival_ms 805; group 18 (latest 30, earlier pages keep place, arrival while reading keeps draft/focus/scroll), 19 (drafts, Enter/Shift+Enter, live seen/unread), 21 (session ended mid-draft) passed. RISK: these are scripted Playwright observations, not a configured claude-code/glm-5.3-flashx judge run; there is no judge transcript in the evidence index showing the judge actually performs the waits, independent-context actions (browser_run_code_unsafe availability in @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 is not verified here) and page.evaluate reads instead of scoring a snapshot, and the functional dimension's long protocol (timeout 9000 s) has no measured workload. Minor note (P3, not a fail): hro_pol_earlier_place says 'scroll to the top of what is shown and note which message is at the top' then 'Bring in earlier messages'; with an auto-load-on-scroll implementation the judge may need to read the anchor before the load fires, but a judge can still anchor on the message that was at the top and compare, so a conforming infinite-scroll app is not clearly failed.
